groups.name: carry
groups.description: segments are formatted in order with one carry, then the outputs are reformatted with a fresh carry and must not change; langs overrides lang per segment

cases.desc: closing quote after an inline element
two pairs across an empty segment
nesting across three segments
apostrophe after a segment boundary
opener in ru closes as ru in an en segment
unsupported-lang segment mid-quote leaves the stack intact
minus after whitespace in the previous segment
minus after a word in the previous segment stays
minus after an opening bracket in the previous segment
quote run at the start of a segment looks past it to the previous segment
zone operator in the previous segment is a lead
line-start dash after a newline in the previous segment
dash after a word in the previous segment stays
numeric range: a word at the end of the previous segment declines
numeric range: a hyphen at the end of the previous segment declines
numeric range: whitespace at the end of the previous segment allows
a double hyphen at the end of a piece is left alone, so the minus in the next piece has no lead

groups.name: carry-boundaries
groups.description: Lookahead rules decide within one piece, so wrong and missed edits at an inline boundary are accepted as one carve-out (readme Scope). Each case pins today's output

cases.desc: numeric range: a hyphen at the end of a piece is not seen as a range (missed edit)
numeric range: a hyphen at the start of a piece is not seen as a range (missed edit)
numeric range: the chain guard cannot see the next piece, so the first pair converts (wrong edit)
apostrophe at the end of a piece is read as a closing quote while a single quote is pending
isolated quote in a piece of its own is read as an opener
a single quote before a number is opened when the number is in the next piece
short-word nbsp: a short word at the end of a piece does not see the space at the start of the next piece (missed edit)
short-word nbsp: an ampersand at the start of a piece has no space before it in the piece (missed edit)
math zone: an operator in a piece that starts with it has no left operand
a quote at the end of the previous piece hides what precedes it, so the minus declines
hyphen: the identifier guard sees only its own piece, so a hostname split by an element is glued (wrong edit)
operator in its own inline piece is not seen
em dash: a spaced dash at the end of a piece has no right neighbor (missed edit)
